title: Nonthermal Particle Acceleration by Magnetic Pumping in Pulsating Plasmas
summary: We present a new "pulsating box" setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-beta plasmas undergoing compression-expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. Numerical results are in excellent agreement with a generalized maximum entropy model that we derive, linking the power-law index of distributions to the injected energy. Our results are relevant for understanding the origin of high-energy particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.

AI.tldr: Introduces a novel simulation and theoretical model showing that magnetic pumping in compressing-expanding high-beta plasmas efficiently accelerates particles, producing power-law energy distributions relevant for astrophysical high-energy particle origins.
AI.motivation: To understand particle acceleration mechanisms in high-beta plasmas undergoing compression-expansion cycles, which is important for explaining high-energy particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.
AI.method: Development of a new 'pulsating box' numerical simulation model that performs fully kinetic simulations of particles in high-beta plasmas experiencing magnetic pumping during compression-expansion cycles; alongside, derivation of a generalized maximum entropy theoretical model to relate power-law indices with injected energy.
AI.result: Simulation results demonstrate efficient particle acceleration by magnetic pumping, yielding nonthermal energy distributions exhibiting power-law tails. The numerical findings closely match predictions from the generalized maximum entropy model linking power-law indices to energy input.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a robust numerical and theoretical framework explaining particle acceleration via magnetic pumping in high-beta plasmas, offering insights into the origin of high-energy particles observed in space and astrophysical environments.

title: Constraining the jet base emission of M87* with past and future Event Horizon Telescope observations
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics; 14 pages, 10 figures
summary: We investigate the detectability of the jet base of M87* at Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observing frequencies. Although M87 is known to host a prominent relativistic jet, detecting jet emission close to the black hole at horizon scales remains challenging. Our goal is to determine the minimum jet intensity that can be reliably detected with the recent EHT array configurations. We use synthetic EHT data generated for three array configurations corresponding to the 2021 and 2022 observing campaigns and to a near future EHT campaign. As input models, we employ semi analytic accretion jet models in which the jet emission can be tuned independently of the accretion flow. The synthetic data are reconstructed with regularized maximum likelihood and Bayesian imaging. Jet detectability is assessed through flux density recovery, image fidelity, and uncertainty maps. We find that jet detectability strongly depends on the jet intensity, the array configuration, and imaging methodology. Using our analysis, we determine a lower limit on the jet intensity that can be reliably recovered. The 2022 EHT array configuration represents a significant improvement over earlier arrays, enabling a more robust reconstruction of faint jet features. Our results indicate that the current EHT array is already sensitive to weak jet emission at horizon scales in M87*. The improved short-baseline coverage introduced in 2022 makes faint inner jet features more easily detectable. If the inner jet contributes a significant fraction of the unresolved compact flux, it should become visible in post-2021 observations. On the other hand, if no clear jet signature is found, this would suggest that the horizon-scale jet contributes only a small part of the compact emission. The continued expansion of the EHT will further improve the detection of such jet emission in M87*.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the detectability of M87* jet emission at horizon scales using synthetic data for EHT arrays. Results show that the 2022 EHT array significantly improves detection sensitivity, making weak inner jet features observable. This informs the understanding of M87*'s jet contribution to compact emission, with future EHT expansions promising further improvements.
AI.motivation: To determine the minimum jet intensity near the black hole M87* that can be reliably detected using the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), addressing the challenge of detecting jet emission at horizon scales despite M87 hosting a prominent relativistic jet.
AI.method: Synthetic EHT data were generated using semi-analytic accretion jet models with tunable jet emission across three EHT array configurations (2021, 2022, and near future). Data were then reconstructed with regularized maximum likelihood and Bayesian imaging techniques. Jet detectability was assessed via flux recovery, image fidelity, and uncertainty analysis.
AI.result: Jet detectability strongly depends on jet intensity, array configuration, and imaging methodology. The 2022 EHT configuration improved detection capabilities compared to earlier arrays, allowing robust reconstruction of faint jet features. Current EHT arrays are sensitive enough to detect weak jet emission at horizon scales. Improved short-baseline coverage enhances detectability of inner jet features, and if no jet is detected post-2021, it implies a minimal contribution of horizon-scale jet emission to compact flux. Further EHT expansion will enhance jet emission detection.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that current and improved EHT array configurations, especially the 2022 setup, enable detection of weak jet emissions close to the black hole in M87*. Detecting or not detecting such emissions informs the contribution of the jet to the compact flux. Continued EHT development will enhance these observational capabilities.

title: The WISSHFUL program: the highest redshift UFO discovered in a non-lensed QSO
summary: We present the first results from the WISSHFUL program, an XMM-Newton heritage program targeting luminous QSOs at Cosmic Noon. We report on recent simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations of the Super-Eddington accreting quasar WISSH13 at z=3.294, which provide the highest quality broadband X-ray spectrum to date for a non-lensed QSO at this redshift. Physical modeling of the continuum reveals a soft photon index ($Γ\sim2$) and strong reflection ($R\sim1.4-1.8$), despite the weak narrow Fe emission, and a low high-energy cut-off ($E_{cut}\sim60-80$ keV, $kTe = 15-20$ keV, depending on the model adopted). Most notably, we detect two significant (at $96.7\%$ and $98.9\%$ confidence level, respectively) absorption features at $\sim7.5$ and $\sim10$ keV rest-frame, interpreted as a blueshifted blend of Fe XXV He$α$ and Fe XXVI Ly$α$. These features indicate the presence of two kinematic components of a highly ionized, high column Ultra-Fast Outflow (UFO) with a velocity of $v_{out}\sim0.1c$ and $v_{out}\sim0.3c$, respectively. The slower wind is consistently detected in an archival 2017 XMM-Newton observation, whereas the faster wind is detected only in 2024. This stratified and variable wind exhibits extreme energetics, with a mass outflow rate of $\dot{M}_{out}\sim20M_{\odot}/yr$ (corresponding to $15\% \dot{M}_{acc}$) for each component, and a kinetic power of the order of $\sim1$ and $\sim10\%$ of the bolometric luminosity, respectively. While this represents one of the most powerful UFOs ever detected, its kinetic power is a similar fraction of the QSO's bolometric luminosity compared to lower-redshift AGN. We present several theoretical frameworks to explain the peculiar accretion and ejection properties of this remarkable QSO at Cosmic Noon.

AI.tldr: High-quality X-ray observations of quasar WISSH13 at z=3.294 reveal a powerful, stratified ultra-fast outflow with velocities up to 0.3c, significant mass outflow rates, and kinetic power up to 10% of the bolometric luminosity, shedding light on extreme accretion and ejection mechanisms at Cosmic Noon.
AI.motivation: To investigate the accretion and ejection properties of luminous QSOs at Cosmic Noon using high-quality broadband X-ray spectra.
AI.method: Simultaneous observations with XMM-Newton and NuSTAR of the Super-Eddington accreting quasar WISSH13 at z=3.294, including physical modeling of the continuum and identification of absorption features.
AI.result: Detection of two significant blueshifted absorption features indicating a stratified Ultra-Fast Outflow with velocities ~0.1c and ~0.3c, mass outflow rate ~20 M_sun/yr for each component, and kinetic power up to ~10% of the bolometric luminosity; the slower wind was consistent in archival data, while the faster wind is newly detected in 2024.
AI.conclusion: WISSH13 exhibits one of the most powerful UFOs ever detected, with extreme energetics comparable in fraction to lower-redshift AGN, and the study offers theoretical scenarios explaining its peculiar super-Eddington accretion and wind properties at Cosmic Noon.

title: How Common Are Common Envelopes? Quantifying Their Role in Forming Gravitational-Wave Sources
comment: Interactive figures and online catalog can be accessed at https://floorbroekgaarden.github.io/Rates_of_Formation_Channels/interactive_figures_and_tables/formation_channel_rates_table.html
summary: A central goal of gravitational-wave astronomy is to use merging binary black hole (BBH), black hole-neutron star (BHNS), and binary neutron star (BNS) systems as fossils to reconstruct the formation and evolution of massive stars across cosmic time. In practice, this inference relies on population-synthesis models that map massive stellar binaries to merging compact objects. However, these models disagree on the dominant orbital-hardening mechanisms within isolated binary evolution, particularly on whether common-envelope (CE) evolution is required. To address this, we compile and systematically compare formation-channel predictions from more than 200 isolated-binary population-synthesis simulations, organized within a unified hierarchical taxonomy. We find that BBH and BHNS formation pathways span nearly the full allowed range from CE-dominated to without-CE-dominated evolution (0-100%), while often predicting similar merger rates, revealing a fundamental degeneracy: merger-rate measurements alone do not uniquely constrain the underlying evolutionary pathways. In contrast, BNS formation proceeds almost exclusively through channels involving at least one CE phase (>90-100%), suggesting CE evolution plays a qualitatively different role in BNS than in BBH and BHNS formation. The relative contributions of with-CE and without-CE pathways are governed primarily by assumptions controlling mass-transfer stability, angular-momentum loss, CE efficiency, and supernova physics, which often act non-linearly and in correlated fashion, such that trends from one-at-a-time parameter variations do not generalize across simulation frameworks. Robust interpretation of gravitational-wave populations will therefore require transparent formation-channel definitions, reproducible analysis pipelines, systematic cross-code comparisons, and observational constraints that extend beyond merger rates alone.

AI.tldr: The paper compares over 200 binary evolution simulations revealing that while BBH and BHNS merger rates cannot uniquely distinguish between CE and non-CE evolutionary pathways, BNS formation almost always involves CE evolution; interpreting gravitational-wave populations requires standardized methods and constraints beyond merger rates.
AI.motivation: To resolve disagreements among population-synthesis models regarding dominant orbital-hardening mechanisms in isolated binary evolution, especially the role of common-envelope (CE) evolution, to better understand massive star formation and evolution via gravitational-wave sources.
AI.method: Compiled and systematically compared formation-channel predictions from over 200 isolated-binary population-synthesis simulations, organized within a unified hierarchical taxonomy, analyzing the relative contributions of CE and non-CE evolution pathways across binary black hole (BBH), black hole-neutron star (BHNS), and binary neutron star (BNS) systems.
AI.result: Found that BBH and BHNS formation pathways cover a broad spectrum from CE-dominated to non-CE-dominated evolution with similar predicted merger rates, indicating degeneracy that merger rates alone cannot constrain evolutionary pathways uniquely; conversely, BNS formation largely requires at least one CE phase, showing CE's distinct role in BNS evolution; identified that mass-transfer stability, angular-momentum loss, CE efficiency, and supernova physics significantly influence pathway contributions in a non-linear and correlated manner.
AI.conclusion: Merger-rate measurements alone are insufficient to uniquely constrain compact binary evolutionary pathways due to fundamental degeneracies in CE and non-CE channel contributions; thus, robust gravitational-wave population interpretations need transparent channel definitions, reproducible analysis pipelines, systematic cross-code comparisons, and additional observational constraints beyond merger rates.

title: The free-streaming length of dark matter from JWST observations of 28 strong gravitational lenses
summary: The formation of gravitationally bound overdensities of dark matter (DM), or \textit{halos}, is a generic prediction of theories with particle DM. We present a measurement of halo properties in 28 quadruple image strong lens systems recently observed by JWST, and use these observations to constrain the free-streaming length, $λ_{\rm{FS}}$, of DM, a quantity that depends on the DM particle mass and formation mechanism. We improve on previous lensing analyses by simultaneously reconstructing extended lensed arcs with image positions and relative magnifications, enhancing sensitivity to perturbations by halos. Our analysis rules out deviations from the predictions of cold dark matter (CDM) on scales above $10^{7.2} M_{\odot}$ and $10^{7.4} M_{\odot}$ for subhalo abundance predicted by cosmological $N$-body simulations and semi-analytic models, respectively. These bounds correspond to upper limits $λ_{\rm{FS}}<6.0 \ \rm{kpc}$ and $λ_{\rm{FS}}<7.0 \ \rm{kpc}$, and lower limits on the mass of a spin--1/2 thermal relic DM particle $m_{\rm{therm}}>7.4 \ \rm{keV}$ and $m_{\rm{therm}}>6.5 \ \rm{keV}$. Conversely, assuming a negligible free-streaming length, as predicted by CDM, we measure a projected mass in subhalos around elliptical galaxies $1.7_{-1.2}^{+2.6} \times 10^7 \ \mathrm{M}_{\odot} \ \rm{kpc^{-2}}$ at $95 \%$ confidence. These inferences confirm key predictions of the CDM paradigm.

AI.tldr: Using JWST observations of 28 strong lens systems, this study constrains dark matter free-streaming length and particle mass by analyzing halo-induced lensing perturbations, confirming predictions of the cold dark matter model and setting limits of free-streaming length below ~7 kpc and particle mass above ~6.5 keV.
AI.motivation: To test key predictions of particle dark matter theories regarding halo formation and constrain dark matter properties such as free-streaming length and particle mass using observational data from strong lensing.
AI.method: Analyzed 28 quadruple image strong lens systems observed by JWST, simultaneously reconstructing extended lensed arcs with image positions and relative magnifications to sensitively detect perturbations by dark matter halos. Used these measurements to constrain free-streaming length and dark matter particle mass, comparing results with cosmological simulations and semi-analytic models.
AI.result: Ruled out deviations from cold dark matter (CDM) predictions for subhalo abundance above approximately 10^{7.2}-10^{7.4} solar masses, setting upper limits on free-streaming length (6.0–7.0 kpc) and lower limits on thermal relic dark matter particle mass (6.5–7.4 keV). Measured a projected subhalo mass density around elliptical galaxies consistent with CDM at 1.7^{+2.6}_{-1.2} × 10^7 M_⊙ kpc^{-2} (95% confidence).
AI.conclusion: The observational analysis supports the cold dark matter paradigm by confirming predicted halo properties and sets stringent constraints on the free-streaming length and particle mass of dark matter, thus validating particle dark matter theories within current measurement sensitivity.

title: Constraining Orbital Eccentricity of a Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidate PKS 2131-0211
summary: A detailed analysis of the decades-long radio light curve of blazar PKS 2131-021 showed epochs of sinusoidal variations in the radio flux density time-series as detailed in O'Neill et al. (2022). The observed sinusoidal flux modulation arises naturally from relativistic Doppler boosting of the jet when the jet-emitting supermassive black hole (SMBH) orbits its companion. For SMBHs in circular orbits, this scenario yields sinusoidal light curves, offering a simple kinematic explanation for the observed variability in PKS 2131-021. We present an approach that incorporates the effects of orbital eccentricity into the Kinematic Orbital model for PKS 2131-021, using the Keplerian parametric solution to describe the SMBH binary orbit. Using the available radio light curve data, we demonstrate that the proposed SMBH binary likely possesses a residual orbital eccentricity, which we constrain through detailed Bayesian parameter estimation studies to be 0.053 \pm 0.015 with a Bayes factor of 3.15 over the circular model. However, when the analysis accounts for the presence of red noise in the data using a Damped Random Walk (DRW) process, the circular model is preferred, giving an eccentricity upper limit of e < 0.15. Nevertheless, our efforts reveal that the Circular+DRW model is strongly favored. This model consistently recovers a coherent periodic signal across all datasets, with the orbital period remaining well-defined even when accounting for broader uncertainties. This analysis incorporated archival observations from the Haystack Observatory, the University of Michigan Radio Astronomy Observatory (UMRAO), and the Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO), spanning the period from 1975 to 2021, compiled by O'Neill et al. (2022).

AI.tldr: This study analyzes decades of radio observations of blazar PKS 2131-021, modeling its SMBH binary orbit to explain sinusoidal flux variations. While slight eccentricity is suggested, accounting for red noise favors a circular orbit model that robustly recovers the observed periodicity.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed sinusoidal variations in the radio flux density of blazar PKS 2131-021 by modeling the orbital dynamics of its supermassive black hole binary system, including effects of orbital eccentricity.
AI.method: Incorporation of orbital eccentricity effects into the kinematic orbital model for the SMBH binary using Keplerian parametric solutions and Bayesian parameter estimation, alongside modeling red noise with a Damped Random Walk process on decades-long radio light curve data.
AI.result: The binary likely has a small residual eccentricity (e=0.053 ± 0.015) favored over a circular orbit with a Bayes factor of 3.15, but when accounting for red noise (DRW process), the circular orbit model is preferred with an eccentricity upper limit of e<0.15. The Circular+DRW model strongly recovers a coherent periodic signal and a well-defined orbital period.
AI.conclusion: The periodic radio flux variations in PKS 2131-021 are best explained by a SMBH binary system in a circular orbit with Doppler boosting effects, where the inclusion of red noise via DRW modeling supports the circular orbit hypothesis with a robust periodic signal.

title: AGN Line-Intensity Mapping: A Probe of Faint Black Holes at Cosmic Noon
summary: We propose line-intensity mapping (LIM) as a new probe of active galactic nuclei (AGN). By cross-correlating [Ne V] intensity maps with galaxy redshift surveys, we show that the cumulative AGN line emission can be detected even when individual sources are below the detection threshold. The 97.1 eV ionization potential of [Ne V] makes it an essentially uncontaminated tracer of AGN activity, arising from the narrow line region which is accessible even in heavily obscured AGN. We forecast signal-to-noise ratios using a Fisher matrix formalism for two hypothetical future instruments: a CDIM-like instrument targeting [Ne V] $λ3426$ and a PRIMA-like instrument optimized for LIM targeting [Ne V] $14.3 μ$m. For the CDIM-like case we find strong constraints on the product of the mean AGN intensity and bias, $S_{\rm NeV} b_{\rm NeV}$, across $z=2-3$, with redshift-space distortions enabling individual constraints on $S_{\rm NeV}$ and $b_{\rm NeV}$. The LIM signal retains sensitivity to AGN below the $5σ$ direct detection threshold, which at $z=3$ corresponds to $L_{\rm bol} \sim 5\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and coincides with the faint end of existing luminosity function measurements. Roughly 10% of the total signal originates from below this threshold, with the sub-threshold population detectable at $S/N=9-4$ across $z=2-3$ (for $S_{\rm NeV} b_{\rm NeV}$). The PRIMA-like instrument achieves slightly lower signal-to-noise but provides a complementary probe of the AGN population due to the insensitivity of the $14.3 μ$m line to dust attenuation. AGN LIM can potentially be applied to several scientific problems including tracing the total AGN emissivity history, constraining the black hole-halo connection at faint luminosities, and discriminating between supermassive black hole seeding mechanisms.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces [Ne V] line-intensity mapping as a novel method to detect cumulative and faint AGN activity, validated through forecasts for future instruments, offering new insights into AGN demographics and evolution beyond individual source detection.
AI.motivation: Current methods struggle to detect faint or obscured AGN populations individually; there is a need for an approach to probe cumulative AGN activity below individual detection thresholds
AI.method: Propose line-intensity mapping of [Ne V] emission, cross-correlated with galaxy redshift surveys, using Fisher matrix forecasts for two hypothetical instruments (CDIM-like and PRIMA-like) targeting different [Ne V] lines
AI.result: Detectable cumulative AGN line emission from sub-threshold sources with significant signal-to-noise ratios; ability to constrain mean AGN intensity and bias, and to probe AGN below traditional detection limits, with complementary benefits between optical and infrared lines
AI.conclusion: LIM of the [Ne V] line is a powerful probe of AGN populations including heavily obscured sources, enabling studies of AGN emissivity history, black hole-halo relations, and black hole seeding scenarios beyond current detection capabilities

title: Complex Analysis of Askaryan Radiation: UHECR Reconstruction with Askaryan Radio Array
summary: Ultra-high energy cosmic rays (UHECR) can produce relativistic cascades that emit radio-frequency (RF) pulses in the 0.05-1 GHz bandwidth via two distinct effects: the geomagnetic effect, and the Askaryan effect. The geomagnetic effect occurs when the magnetic field of the Earth causes cascade charges to form a transverse current that radiates linearly polarized radiation aligned with the Lorentz force direction. The Askaryan effect is caused by the net negative charge excess in the cascade that radiates linearly polarized radiation along the Cherenkov cone. When UHECR cascades enter solid, RF transparent matter at altitudes where the cascade develops, Askaryan radiation can propagate through the solid matter to RF detectors. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) at the South Pole has observed 13 UHECR candidates in precisely this fashion. We present an analytical model that confirms the events are UHECRs. The model includes Askaryan radiation and the ARA RF channel response. The coherently summed waveforms (CSWs) from the UHECR candidates match our model with correlation coefficients between 0.69 and 0.86, and with minimal fractional power differences. Finally, we demonstrate how to use the analytic formalism to obtain the Askaryan $\vec{E}$-field, and that it matches the results from ARA.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an analytical model confirming the detection of ultra-high energy cosmic rays through Askaryan radiation in radio-frequency pulses recorded by the Askaryan Radio Array at the South Pole, demonstrating strong agreement between modeled and observed signals.
AI.motivation: To confirm the observation of ultra-high energy cosmic rays (UHECR) via radio-frequency pulses and provide a solid analytical model for the detected signals.
AI.method: Develop an analytical model incorporating Askaryan radiation and ARA RF channel response to simulate the coherently summed waveforms from UHECR candidates.
AI.result: The model confirms 13 observed UHECR candidate events at the South Pole, with waveform correlations between 0.69 and 0.86 and minimal power differences, successfully matching the Askaryan electric field measurements from ARA.
AI.conclusion: The analytical model validates the detection of UHECRs via Askaryan radiation observed by ARA, providing a reliable approach to identify and analyze these high-energy cosmic events through RF measurements.

title: The DESI results impact the local determination of $H_0$
summary: Measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) have revealed evidence for dark energy that evolves. If local distance measurements are analyzed with the $w_0w_a$ models preferred by the DESI measurements, the value for the Hubble constant can be as much as $2.5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ smaller than the value obtained assuming $Λ$CDM. When these $w_0w_a$ models are further constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernova (SNIa) data, the downward shift is $1.1 \pm 0.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ (DESI + CMB) and $0.5 \pm 0.1\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ (DESI + CMB + SNIa). The dependence of local determinations of $H_0$ on the background cosmology, combined with the fact that the low-redshift cosmology is not well constrained, is relevant to the Hubble tension.

AI.tldr: DESI BAO measurements support evolving dark energy models that reduce the local Hubble constant value relative to ΛCDM, with combined CMB and SNIa data confirming this downward shift, pointing to the cosmological model dependence as a factor in the Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to address the evolving nature of dark energy and its impact on local measurements of the Hubble constant, particularly in the context of the observed Hubble tension.
AI.method: The study analyzes baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) data from DESI, and constrains cosmological models ($w_0w_a$) using cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernova (SNIa) data to refine estimates of the Hubble constant.
AI.result: The analysis shows that adopting evolving dark energy models ($w_0w_a$) can reduce the local Hubble constant value by up to 2.5 km/s/Mpc compared to the ΛCDM model. When combined with CMB and SNIa data, the downward shift is smaller but significant, indicating sensitivity of $H_0$ to background cosmology and implying relevance to the Hubble tension problem.
AI.conclusion: The dependence of local $H_0$ measurements on the assumed cosmological model, especially the nature of dark energy, suggests that unresolved low-redshift cosmology constraints contribute to the Hubble tension, highlighting the importance of considering evolving dark energy in cosmological analyses.

title: Joint Multi-Period Fermi-LAT and LHAASO Constraints on Axion-Like Particles from Mrk 421 Using Profile Likelihood with Gaussian Copula Correlation
comment: Ready to submit; comments are welcome
summary: We construct a multi-epoch joint profile-likelihood framework to constrain axion-like particles (ALPs), employing a Gaussian copula ($ρ=0.03$) to account for weak correlations among distinct observational periods. Different from traditional independent likelihood addition, our scheme globally optimizes nuisance parameters under the no-ALP hypothesis prior to profiling ALP mass $m_a$ and coupling $g_{aγ}$, enhancing numerical stability and statistical consistency. Using five sets of simultaneous Fermi-LAT and LHAASO data of Mrk 421, we implement both two-zone hybrid and single-zone hadronic jet models. In the CAST-sensitive low-mass regime $m_a\lesssim1$ neV, the 95\% CL upper limit of $g_{aγ}$ is $8.33\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Over $0.1$-$500$ neV, conservative bounds read $g_{aγ}<6.50\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ (two-zone) and $g_{aγ}<7.30\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ (single-zone). These results benefit from LHAASO's broadband very high energy coverage and long term monitoring of Mrk 421; the developed framework provides a robust and scalable pipeline suitable for future multi-messenger ALP searches with next-generation gamma-ray observatories.

AI.tldr: This work introduces a robust multi-epoch statistical framework utilizing gamma-ray observations to set stringent constraints on axion-like particle properties, improving upon traditional methods by accounting for inter-epoch correlations and optimizing nuisance parameters globally.
AI.motivation: To improve constraints on axion-like particles (ALPs) by addressing correlations across multiple observational epochs and enhancing statistical robustness in analysis.
AI.method: Developed a multi-epoch joint profile-likelihood framework using a Gaussian copula to model weak correlations between observational periods, globally optimizing nuisance parameters under the no-ALP hypothesis before profiling ALP parameters, and applying both two-zone hybrid and single-zone hadronic jet models to multi-instrument gamma-ray data of Mrk 421.
AI.result: Obtained stringent upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling over a broad mass range, achieving a 95% confidence level limit of $8.33\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a\lesssim1$ neV and conservative bounds up to $7.30\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ over $0.1$-$500$ neV, leveraging LHAASO's broad energy coverage and extended monitoring.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers a numerically stable, statistically consistent, and scalable approach to jointly analyze multi-epoch gamma-ray data for ALP searches, significantly enhancing sensitivity and suitability for future multi-messenger observations with next-generation gamma-ray observatories.

title: On the potential for inhomogeneities to mimic an evolving dark energy
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, submitted to PRD. Comments welcome
summary: In this work we explore the ability of inhomogeneities to result in an apparent dynamical evolution of dark energy. The idea that inhomogeneities may alter the expansion history of the Universe is not a new one. However, with the current excitement surrounding the inferred time-evolution of the equation of state of dark energy by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and supernovae observations, it is worth revisiting. We use numerical relativity simulations of large-scale structure formation combined with nonlinear general-relativistic ray tracing to infer dark energy parameters for synthetic observers. We adopt a simplified set-up to roughly mimic the observational properties of the DESI plus supernovae and CMB constraints. In our small sample of 20 observers, we find one who infers parameters consistent with the DESI values at 2-$σ$ significance. While it is rare in our limited sample size, we show that it is at least possible for observers to infer significant non-LCDM parameters when their universe is well-described by a cosmological constant on average.

AI.tldr: This study uses numerical relativity and ray tracing to show that cosmic inhomogeneities can cause observers to infer evolving dark energy parameters, highlighting that observed deviations from the cosmological constant might result from local universe structure rather than actual dark energy dynamics.
AI.motivation: Revisit the impact of inhomogeneities on the apparent dynamical evolution of dark energy due to recent findings suggesting time-evolution of dark energy's equation of state from DESI, CMB, and supernovae data.
AI.method: Conduct numerical relativity simulations of large-scale structure formation with nonlinear general-relativistic ray tracing to emulate observational conditions similar to DESI plus supernovae and CMB, analyzing inferred dark energy parameters from synthetic observers.
AI.result: Among 20 synthetic observers, one inferred dark energy parameters consistent with DESI's non-LCDM values at 2-sigma significance, indicating that such parameter inferences, though rare, are possible even when the universe is fundamentally described by a cosmological constant.
AI.conclusion: Inhomogeneities in the universe can lead to apparent observations of dynamically evolving dark energy parameters, suggesting that the inferred time-evolution of dark energy could be an observational artifact rather than a true deviation from the cosmological constant model.

title: The X-ray emission of the long-period transient and accreting cataclysmic variable ASKAP J174508.9-505149
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A Letters on 27/05/2026. 7 pages (4 main text+ 3 appendices)
summary: Long-period transients (LPTs) challenge our knowledge of the mechanism producing radio periodic pulsations in compact objects. Some LPTs have been associated with systems hosting a white dwarf and a low-mass star in a detached binary. Recently, a new LPT (ASKAP\,J174508.9-505149) has been classified as an accreting cataclysmic variable (CV). In the present letter, we report on the detailed study of the X-ray variability of ASKAP\,J174508.9-505149 as observed by \emph{XMM-Newton} and \emph{Einstein Probe} between September 2025 and May 2026. Simultaneous optical and radio observations are also presented. We studied the timing variability of the source, and estimated an X-ray periodicity of $P=4868(22)$\,s, consistent with radio and optical periods. We also observe the same periodicity in the hardness ratio extracted from the \emph{XMM-Newton} observation, peaking at the minimum of the modulation. A long-term modulation is also present in the X-rays and in the B-band photometry, but it is poorly constrained by the current dataset. Spectral X-ray analysis shows the presence of a black-body component ($\sim$0.1\,keV), a collisionally ionised plasma ($\sim$15\,keV), and an absorption feature at 0.77 keV (possibly due to Oxygen-VII). This is the third LPT detected in the X-ray band, the second with a detected X-ray periodicity and variable X-ray emission, and the first conclusively recognised as an accreting magnetic CV.

AI.tldr: This study presents multi-wavelength observations of ASKAP J174508.9-505149, identifying its X-ray periodicity and spectral features, confirming it as an accreting magnetic cataclysmic variable and contributing to the understanding of long-period transients in compact binary systems.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanism producing long-period transients (LPTs) in compact objects, particularly those associated with white dwarf and low-mass star binaries, by studying a newly classified accreting cataclysmic variable.
AI.method: Detailed study of X-ray variability using observations from XMM-Newton and Einstein Probe from Sept 2025 to May 2026, supplemented with simultaneous optical and radio observations; timing variability and spectral X-ray analyses were conducted.
AI.result: Discovered an X-ray periodicity of approximately 4868 seconds consistent with radio and optical periods; identified the same periodicity in the hardness ratio; observed long-term modulation in X-ray and optical bands; confirmed spectral components including a black-body, collisionally ionized plasma, and an absorption feature possibly due to Oxygen-VII; classified the source as an accreting magnetic cataclysmic variable.
AI.conclusion: ASKAP J174508.9-505149 represents the third LPT detected in X-rays, with clear detection of X-ray periodicity and variability, establishing it as the first conclusively identified accreting magnetic cataclysmic variable among LPTs, advancing understanding of LPT mechanisms in compact binaries.

title: Dissipative Cosmology and the Nature of Dark Energy: Insights from Bulk Viscosity with DESI DR2 observations
summary: We explore a cosmological model in which dark energy is described by a bulk viscous fluid, providing a dissipative mechanism for late-time cosmic acceleration. Considering both minimally and non-minimally coupled scenarios, we constrain the model using SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and Planck 2018 CMB data. We find that viscous effects can successfully mimic dynamical dark energy and yield improved fits over $Λ$CDM, particularly in the interacting non-minimal case. Our results demonstrate that dissipative processes offer a viable and physically motivated alternative to the cosmological constant in explaining the current accelerated expansion of the universe.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates bulk viscous fluid models for dark energy, constrained by cosmological observations, showing they can better explain late-time cosmic acceleration than ΛCDM, particularly when non-minimal coupling and interaction are considered.
AI.motivation: To explore alternative explanations for late-time cosmic acceleration beyond the cosmological constant by introducing dissipative mechanisms through bulk viscous dark energy models.
AI.method: Consideration of both minimally and non-minimally coupled bulk viscous dark energy scenarios, with constraints derived from observational datasets including SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and Planck 2018 CMB data.
AI.result: Viscous effects in the dark energy fluid can effectively mimic dynamical dark energy and provide improved fits to observational data compared to the standard ΛCDM model, especially in the interacting non-minimally coupled case.
AI.conclusion: Dissipative processes modeled by bulk viscous fluids constitute a viable and physically motivated alternative to the cosmological constant for explaining the observed accelerated expansion of the universe.

title: Modeling Gamma-Ray Burst Spectra with Convolutional Neural Networks: Fast-Cooling Synchrotron Emission in a Decaying Magnetic Field
comment: 20 pages, 9 figures,accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The radiation mechanism of gamma-ray burst (GRB) prompt emission remains uncertain. Although the fast-cooling synchrotron model in a decaying magnetic field can account for the characteristic nonthermal spectral shape, its computational cost has limited its use in systematic observational fitting and statistical model comparison. We develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based spectral emulator for this physical model and train it on a large synthetic data set generated over a physically motivated parameter space. The trained network reproduces the numerical spectra with high fidelity while reducing the cost of spectral evaluation to the millisecond level. We then incorporate the emulator into a Bayesian spectral-analysis framework and apply it to the time-resolved spectra of GRB 231020A observed by Fermi/GBM. In most time intervals, the decaying-field fast-cooling synchrotron model provides better fits and smaller Bayesian information criterion values than the standard fast-cooling synchrotron model. These results suggest that a radially decaying magnetic field provides a plausible and more physically motivated interpretation of the prompt-emission spectrum of this burst, while also indicating that the emulator offers a practical route for large-sample Bayesian inference and systematic comparisons of GRB prompt-emission models.

AI.tldr: A CNN-based emulator for the fast-cooling synchrotron model in a decaying magnetic field accelerates spectral fitting, improving model comparison for GRB prompt emission; applied to GRB 231020A, it supports the decaying-field scenario as a better physical model.
AI.motivation: The uncertainty in the radiation mechanism of gamma-ray burst (GRB) prompt emission and the high computational cost of the fast-cooling synchrotron model in a decaying magnetic field, which limits systematic observational fitting and model comparison.
AI.method: Development of a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based spectral emulator trained on a large synthetic data set covering a physically motivated parameter space, integrated into a Bayesian spectral-analysis framework for time-resolved spectra fitting.
AI.result: The CNN emulator reproduces numerical spectra with high accuracy while drastically reducing evaluation time to milliseconds. Application to GRB 231020A data shows the decaying-field fast-cooling synchrotron model fits better and yields lower Bayesian information criterion values than the standard model.
AI.conclusion: A radially decaying magnetic field is a plausible and physically motivated explanation for the prompt-emission spectrum of GRB 231020A. The CNN emulator enables practical, large-sample Bayesian inference and systematic model comparisons for GRB prompt emission studies.

title: Metastability in Emergent Dark Energy: A New Framework Confronting Cosmological Observations
summary: We propose the Metastable Emergent Dark Energy (MEDE) model, a novel phenomenological extension of the Phenomenological (PEDE) and Generalized (GEDE) Emergent Dark Energy frameworks, in which dark energy exhibits a transitionary behavior, appearing at late times and vanishing toward the future. This model naturally enables a smooth crossing of the phantom divide line in the dark energy equation of state, as hinted at by recent observations. The MEDE model is defined by a hyperbolic tangent dark energy equation of state $w(z)=-1-Δ\tanh[\log_{10}((1+z)/(1+z_t))]$, introducing only two free parameters, the transition redshift $z_t$ and the variation amplitude $Δ$, allowing both the emergent and transitionary behavior of dark energy. We constrain the MEDE model using a combined dataset of Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and different compilations of Type Ia supernovae, obtaining $z_t=0.425^{+0.084}_{-0.120}$ and $Δ=0.87^{+0.29}_{-0.35}$ (for CMB+DESI+PantheonPlus), indicating a statistically significant deviation from the cosmological constant. Statistical comparisons show that the MEDE model is preferred over $Λ$CDM by the combined dataset, with $Δ\rm DIC_{ MEDE-ΛCDM}= -9.29$. The MEDE model performs comparably to the CPL dynamical dark energy parametrization ($Δ\rm DIC_{MEDE-CPL} = 0.74$), with no strong statistical distinction from CPL using current data. Notably, MEDE preserves the success of $Λ$CDM in describing early-universe physics and naturally accommodates the phantom-crossing signature indicated by the latest low-redshift observations. The MEDE scenario provides a compelling dark energy phenomenology that may guide us toward interesting theoretical implications.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes the MEDE model, extending emergent dark energy concepts with a transitionary equation of state. It fits various cosmological data better than $Λ$CDM, supports phantom crossing, and remains competitive with CPL models, providing new insights into dark energy behavior.
AI.motivation: To address observational hints of dark energy's phantom divide line crossing and to extend emergent dark energy frameworks with a model exhibiting transitionary late-time behavior.
AI.method: Introduced the Metastable Emergent Dark Energy (MEDE) model characterized by a hyperbolic tangent equation of state with two free parameters, constrained using Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Type Ia supernova data.
AI.result: MEDE parameters were constrained to $z_t=0.425^{+0.084}_{-0.120}$ and $Δ=0.87^{+0.29}_{-0.35}$, showing a statistically significant deviation from the cosmological constant and preferred over $Λ$CDM by combined data; performance comparable to CPL parametrization with no strong statistical difference.
AI.conclusion: The MEDE model successfully describes a late-time transitionary dark energy behavior allowing phantom divide crossing, preserves early-universe physics, is statistically favored over $Λ$CDM, and offers promising theoretical implications in dark energy phenomenology.

title: Simulations of interaction between outflow and surrounding broken power-law circumnuclear medium: implications for different radio light curves of TDEs
summary: The complex radio light curves of tidal disruption events (TDEs) challenge our understanding of the properties of both the outflows and the circumnuclear medium (CNM) surrounding supermassive black holes. In this work, we explore outflow-CNM interactions across a broad parameter space using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations, adopting a broken power-law CNM density profile with a transition near the Bondi radius. The outflow-CNM interaction inside Bondi radius produces an early radio flare (\(\lesssim 2\) yr) once the emitting region becomes optically thin. A second radio rebrightening can appear a few years later if the outflow decelerates beyond Bondi radius. We also find that either a very dense inner CNM, which causes rapid deceleration, or a rarefied outer CNM suppresses the late rebrightening that will produces a single early-peaked flare. In contrast, a rarefied CNM inside the Bondi radius suppresses the early flare and yields a single late-peaked event. For the case of very dense CNM at large radii, the interaction will trigger a sharp late-time rise as observed in some TDEs. We further explore the interaction of a relativistic jet with a broken power-law CNM, which can reproduce the characteristic light curves as observed in jetted TDEs without invoking complex jet structure.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 3D hydrodynamic simulations to show that interactions between TDE outflows and a broken power-law CNM density profile, with a transition near the Bondi radius, explain the timing and shape of early and late radio flares, including those from relativistic jets.
AI.motivation: To understand the complex radio light curves of tidal disruption events (TDEs) by investigating the properties of outflows and the circumnuclear medium (CNM) around supermassive black holes.
AI.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of outflow-CNM interactions using a broken power-law CNM density profile with a transition near the Bondi radius.
AI.result: The study reveals that the CNM density structure inside and outside the Bondi radius governs early and late radio flares in TDEs. Dense inner CNM causes early flares, while rarefied inner CNM suppresses them, producing late-peaked flares. Dense outer CNM leads to sharp late-time rises. These interactions also explain jetted TDE light curves without complex jet structures.
AI.conclusion: The complex radio light curves of TDEs can be explained by outflow-CNM interactions shaped by a broken power-law CNM density profile. This provides a unified framework to interpret early and late radio flares, including those from relativistic jets, enhancing our understanding of TDE environments and outflow dynamics.

title: Reconstructing dark energy with fewer assumptions
summary: We perform minimalistic reconstructions of the dark energy density and equation of state using late-time distance measurements. Our methodology avoids assumptions that correlate the values of these functions over time and instead yields their approximate average evolution within seven redshift bins from $z=0$ to $z=4.2$. Constraints are obtained using combinations of BAO measurements from DESI and SDSS, alongside Type Ia supernovae measurements from Pantheon+ and the latest recalibrated samples, Union3.1 and DES-Dovekie. Only an acoustic scale prior is included from the CMB so that our results are insensitive to the possible matter density tension between early and late-time probes. All combinations yield consistent reconstructed histories: a dark energy density that rises to a local maximum before decreasing at late times and an equation of state with two apparent oscillations around the cosmological constant limit. Both functions tentatively suggest a phantom crossing in the equation of state around $z\sim0.6$-$0.8$. These patterns are robust to numerous parameter extensions, such as freely varying spatial curvature and neutrino mass, and they persist in the uncorrelated amplitudes obtained through localized principal component analysis. Deviations from $Λ$CDM in individual bins reach a maximum significance of $\sim2.6$-$3σ$, while the total chi-square difference between the reconstructions and this model provides up to $\sim2σ$ support for the seven additional parameters in the reconstructions. As these significances remain moderate, our main result is the level of consistency between combinations of the most widely used background-level observations. Our results suggest that the dark energy evolution signal is a persistent feature of the data and that it cannot be explained solely by fluctuations or systematics in individual measurements.

AI.tldr: Using BAO and supernova data, this paper reconstructs dark energy evolution without strong assumptions, revealing a moderately significant time-varying dark energy density and equation of state with possible phantom crossing, consistent across datasets and robust against modeling choices.
AI.motivation: To investigate the possible time evolution of dark energy density and its equation of state using late-time cosmological probes, avoiding assumptions that enforce temporal correlations, in order to address tensions and uncertainties present in standard ΛCDM cosmology and to assess whether observed deviations could be genuine features or artifacts of systematics.
AI.method: The authors perform model-independent, minimalistic reconstructions of the dark energy density and equation of state across seven redshift bins (z=0 to 4.2) using late-time distance measurements from BAO (DESI, SDSS) and Type Ia supernovae (Pantheon+, Union3.1, DES-Dovekie). They include only an acoustic scale prior from the CMB to minimize early-to-late matter density tension effects. Localized principal component analysis is used to extract uncorrelated amplitudes and test robustness against parameter extensions such as spatial curvature and neutrino mass variations.
AI.result: The reconstructed dark energy density shows a rise to a local maximum before declining at late times. The equation of state displays two oscillations around the cosmological constant value, with indications of a phantom crossing near z~0.6–0.8. These features are consistent across multiple data combinations and robust to model extensions. Deviations from ΛCDM reach up to ~2.6–3σ in individual bins, with an overall ~2σ statistical preference for the extended model parameters. The findings suggest that the evolving dark energy signal is persistent and not solely due to measurement fluctuations or systematics.
AI.conclusion: The study finds a consistent, persistent signal of time-evolving dark energy density and equation of state from late-time cosmological data, with features such as a local maximum in density and oscillations in the equation of state, including a tentative phantom crossing near redshift 0.6–0.8. These deviations from ΛCDM are of moderate statistical significance and robust against model extensions and systematic uncertainties.

title: Detectability of secondary images from flares near Sgr A* with mock GRAVITY data
summary: The orbital motion of near-infrared flares reported by the GRAVITY collaboration encodes information about both the dynamics of accretion matter and the underlying spacetime geometry. The centroid track of these flares, which corresponds to the flux-weighted center of light, incorporates contributions from primary, secondary and higher-order images. Thus, it potentially indicates distinctive signatures of the spacetime geometry, even when these individual multiple images remain unresolved. In this study, we explore the detectability of the secondary images from flares orbiting Sgr A* through mock data simulating future GRAVITY observations. Specifically, we compare the model in which the centroid coincides with the track of the primary images with another model in which the centroid incorporates flux-weighted contributions from both the primary and secondary images. Fitting these models to the mock data based on Bayesian framework, we quantify the conditions under which the signature of secondary images can be statistically distinguishable. We demonstrate that increasing the sample size by an order of magnitude alone could not yield strong evidence for distinguishing the secondary image. Robust detectability ($|Δ\text{BIC}| >7.9$) is achieved when both with the improved sample size and astrometric uncertainties reduced to 40\% of current uncertainties of GRAVITY astrometric data. Unlike the primary image, which is dominated by accretion flow physics, the secondary images originate from gravitational lensing in the strong-field regime. Their detection is an essential first step toward probing higher-order images and the photon rings.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the detectability of secondary gravitational lensing images in near-infrared flares around Sgr A* using simulated GRAVITY data, concluding that both increased data quantity and improved astrometric precision are necessary for robust identification, enhancing our ability to test strong-field spacetime geometry.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether secondary images from near-infrared flares orbiting Sgr A* can be detected, thereby providing insights into spacetime geometry beyond primary accretion flow dynamics.
AI.method: Simulated mock data mimicking future GRAVITY observations were generated to compare models of centroid tracks including only primary images versus those including both primary and secondary images, using Bayesian model fitting to assess distinguishability.
AI.result: The study found that increasing sample size alone is insufficient for robust detection; a combination of a larger sample size and a 60% reduction in astrometric uncertainties is required to statistically distinguish secondary images with strong evidence.
AI.conclusion: Detecting secondary images from flares orbiting Sgr A* is feasible with improved observational precision and sample size, which would serve as a crucial step toward probing strong-field gravitational lensing effects such as higher-order images and photon rings.

title: AKRA 3.0: A matrix-free Inversion Framework for Weak Lensing Mass Mapping and Its Application to DES Y3 Data
summary:
Weak gravitational lensing mass mapping offers a direct probe of the matter distribution.
  Accurate reconstruction of mass maps from masked shear catalogs remains challenging due to survey boundaries and spatially varying noise. In AKRA 2.0, we addressed the mask problem on the curved sky by constructing and inverting the normal-equation matrix $\bf{H} \equiv \mathbf{A}^\mathrm{T}\mathbf{N}^{-1} \mathbf{A}$ explicitly, necessitating a split-scale strategy that reconstructed different angular scales independently to reach high resolution.
  Here we present AKRA 3.0, in which $\mathbf{H}$ is treated as a linear operator and the normal equations are solved by the conjugate gradient (CG) method. This reformulation reduces the memory requirement from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$ and the inversion cost from $O(N^3)$ to $O(N_{\rm iter}N^{3/2}), N \sim \ell_{\rm{max}}^2$ for full-sky (SHT-based) operations. Such optimizations render high-resolution full-sky reconstruction tractable for Stage~III and Stage~IV surveys.
  Applying AKRA 3.0 to the DES Y3 \texttt{METACALIBRATION} catalog, we produce the highest-resolution convergence map of this dataset to date at HEALPix $N_{\rm{nside}}= 2048$ without imposing any prior assumptions.
  We extract the convergence power spectrum directly from the reconstructed map and demonstrate that unbiased two-point measurements can be obtained directly from the reconstructed map. The reconstructed E-mode convergence map will be publicly released as data products to enable future studies of non-Gaussian statistics, higher-order moments, and cross-correlations with external datasets.

AI.tldr: AKRA 3.0 introduces a computationally efficient conjugate gradient approach for high-resolution weak lensing mass map reconstruction from masked shear data, demonstrated on DES Y3 data to produce high-quality full-sky convergence maps enabling advanced cosmological analyses.
AI.motivation: Accurate reconstruction of weak gravitational lensing mass maps from masked shear catalogs is challenging due to survey boundaries and spatially varying noise, especially on the curved sky.
AI.method: AKRA 3.0 treats the normal-equation matrix as a linear operator and solves it using the conjugate gradient method, reducing memory and computational costs compared to explicit matrix inversion in AKRA 2.0, enabling high-resolution full-sky reconstructions.
AI.result: Successfully applied AKRA 3.0 to DES Y3 METACALIBRATION data to produce the highest-resolution convergence map at HEALPix Nside=2048 without priors, and extracted unbiased two-point measurements directly from the map.
AI.conclusion: The new method allows efficient and accurate high-resolution full-sky weak lensing mass mapping from masked data, facilitating future analyses of non-Gaussian statistics and cross-correlations with external datasets.

title: Probing a new subclass of llGRB-SN transients: Insights from EP250304a and its associated supernova
summary: With the advent of the Einstein Probe (EP) mission, we are entering a new era in the study of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), enabling the detection of faint, low-luminosity transients that would previously have gone undetected. EP250304a was an event discovered by EP associated with the broad-lined type Ic supernova (SN) SN 2025fhm located at z = 0.2. Despite no gamma-ray emission being detected at the time of the EP trigger, we identify evidence for a relativistic outflow consistent with a GRB-like jet across multiple wavelengths. We present a detailed spectral and photometric analysis of EP250304a/SN 2025fhm, including multi-band light curve modelling performed with the Redback Python package. We find that this event closely resembles low-luminosity GRB-SNe (llGRB-SNe) such as GRB 060218/SN 2006aj, GRB 100316D/SN 2010bh, and GRB 171205A/SN 2017iuk, all of which exhibit early-time emission consistent with a thermal shocked cocoon. These similarities suggest that EP250304A/SN 2025fhm may belong to an emerging subclass of shocked cocoon-dominated llGRB-SNe, representing the low-luminosity end of a broader continuum of engine-driven GRB-SN explosions.

AI.tldr: The Einstein Probe detected a faint gamma-ray burst supernova, EP250304a/SN 2025fhm, showing features consistent with low-luminosity GRB-SNe and thermal shocked cocoons, indicating a new subclass of engine-driven GRB-SN explosions.
AI.motivation: To explore faint, low-luminosity gamma-ray burst supernovae (llGRB-SNe) enabled by the new Einstein Probe mission, addressing previously undetectable transient events.
AI.method: Detection of event EP250304a by the Einstein Probe, spectral and photometric analysis including multi-band light curve modeling using the Redback Python package across multiple wavelengths.
AI.result: Identification of EP250304a/SN 2025fhm as a low-luminosity GRB-SN resembling known llGRB-SNe with early thermal shocked cocoon emission, suggesting it is part of a subclass dominated by shocked cocoons representing the low-luminosity end of engine-driven GRB-SN explosions.
AI.conclusion: EP250304a/SN 2025fhm exemplifies a new subclass of low-luminosity GRB-SNe characterized by relativistic outflows and thermal shocked cocoons, expanding the known continuum of engine-driven GRB-SN events enabled by improved detection capabilities of the Einstein Probe.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Probing new signatures of ultralight axions with gravitational lensing
summary: Ultralight axions (ULAs) are well-motivated dark matter particle candidates that arise in many extensions of the Standard Model of particle physics. ULAs with mass $m_\mathrm{a} \lesssim 10^{-27}$ eV have been strongly constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations in temperature and polarization. We fit recent measurements of gravitational lensing of the CMB from \textit{Planck}, the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and the South Pole Telescope (SPT-3G) using a state-of-the-art simulation-calibrated nonlinear clustering model for ULAs. We derive the strongest constraints on ULAs in the mass range $10^{-26}\;\mathrm{eV}\leq m_\mathrm{a}\leq 10^{-24.5}\;\mathrm{eV}$. ULAs of this mass have been shown to alleviate tensions between inferences of the matter clustering if they compose a few percent of the total dark matter content of the Universe. We conclude that ULAs with a mass of $10^{-26}$ eV make up less than 1.5\% of the dark matter and $10^{-25}$ eV axions make less than 9\% (both at 95\% confidence level). We identify a slight preference for non-zero axion density at $10^{-24.5}$ eV at $2.1σ$. We find that the preference for ULAs is largely driven by a few data points and that further investigation of non-linear ULA physics is needed to confirm or rule out this signal.

AI.tldr: Using recent CMB lensing data and nonlinear models, the paper places stringent limits on ultralight axion dark matter fractional abundance between 10^-26 and 10^-24.5 eV, seeing a weak 2.1σ indication of axions at 10^-24.5 eV that requires more study.
AI.motivation: Ultralight axions are promising dark matter candidates but their parameter space is constrained by cosmic microwave background observations; the study aims to provide improved constraints using recent CMB gravitational lensing data.
AI.method: The authors fit measurements of CMB gravitational lensing from Planck, ACT, and SPT-3G with a simulation-calibrated nonlinear clustering model tailored for ULAs.
AI.result: They set the strongest constraints on ULAs in the mass range 10^-26 eV to 10^-24.5 eV, limiting their dark matter fraction to less than 1.5% at 10^-26 eV and less than 9% at 10^-25 eV (95% confidence). They observe a tentative (2.1σ) non-zero axion density signal at 10^-24.5 eV, driven by limited data points.
AI.conclusion: Current CMB lensing data restricts ULA dark matter abundance to low fractions in the specified mass range, with a marginal hint of signal needing further investigation and refinement of non-linear ULA physics.

title: A micronova burst in the intermediate polar IGR J17014-4306
summary: We report the detection of a short optical burst in TESS data of IGR J17014-4306, the eclipsing intermediate polar with the longest known orbital period. The burst lasts 1.56 d and shows multiple peaks, reaching $(9.3 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{33}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and releases a total energy of $(3.25 \pm 0.01) \times 10^{38}$ erg. The burst parameters are consistent with those of a micronova eruption, currently understood as a thermonuclear runaway in the magnetically-confined accretion column. From its energy, we infer a burned column mass of $\sim 1.6 \times 10^{-11}$ M$_\odot$, which implies a recurrence time of $\sim 20$ d. Our search for similar events in long-term Gaia, ASAS-SN, and AAVSO light curves reveals 16 possible fast brightenings over $\sim 11$ yr, suggesting that micronova events may be frequent in IGR J17014-4306. Timing analysis of the TESS data shows that the white-dwarf spin period remains stable before and after the burst. During the burst, however, the power spectrum becomes more complex and exhibits multiple peaks. The classification of IGR J17014-4306 as a micronova brings the total number of confirmed systems to eight. Its extreme orbital period and eclipsing nature make it an ideal test-bed for further studies of magnetically confined thermonuclear burning on white dwarfs.

AI.tldr: The study reports the detection of a micronova eruption in the eclipsing intermediate polar IGR J17014-4306 using TESS data, identifying multiple bursts over years, stable white-dwarf spin periods, and variable power spectra during bursts, highlighting its significance for studying magnetically confined thermonuclear burning on white dwarfs.
AI.motivation: To investigate the occurrence and characteristics of micronova eruptions in the eclipsing intermediate polar IGR J17014-4306, especially given its status as the system with the longest known orbital period, aiming to contribute to understanding magnetically confined thermonuclear burning on white dwarfs.
AI.method: Analyzed TESS optical data to detect bursts, measured burst duration, energy, and luminosity, inferred physical parameters such as burned column mass and recurrence time, and conducted a search for similar events in long-term Gaia, ASAS-SN, and AAVSO light curves. Additionally, performed timing analysis on TESS data to study white-dwarf spin period and power spectrum changes during bursts.
AI.result: Detected a 1.56-day optical burst consistent with a micronova eruption, with peak luminosity of (9.3 ± 0.2) × 10^33 erg s^-1 and total energy release of (3.25 ± 0.01) × 10^38 erg. Inferred burned column mass ∼1.6 × 10^-11 M☉ and recurrence time ∼20 days. Identified 16 possible fast brightenings over ~11 years, suggesting frequent micronovae in this system. White-dwarf spin period remains stable before and after bursts, but the power spectrum complexity increases during bursts. This confirms IGR J17014-4306 as the eighth known micronova system.
AI.conclusion: IGR J17014-4306 exhibits micronova eruptions characterized by magnetically confined thermonuclear runaways, with frequent fast brightenings and stable spin behavior, making it an excellent candidate for further detailed studies of such phenomena in white dwarfs, especially due to its long orbital period and eclipsing nature.

title: Phenomenology of Inflaton-Driven Early QCD Confinement and Solution to Axion Isocurvature Problem
summary: We study the phenomenology of early QCD confinement during inflation, driven by a direct coupling between the inflaton and Standard Model gluons. This coupling dynamically raises the QCD confinement scale, making the axion sufficiently heavy to suppress isocurvature perturbations during the CMB epoch. As inflation proceeds, the confinement scale decreases and the axion becomes light, allowing de Sitter fluctuations during the late stages of inflation or post-inflationary thermal fluctuations to generate the observed dark matter abundance. In addition, QCD-induced corrections to the inflationary potential can shift the scalar spectral index towards smaller values, providing a further observational handle. We embed this mechanism in an $α$-attractor model of inflation and explore the resulting parameter space. We show that, in the minimal scenario with reheating into gluons, successful dark matter production requires deconfinement to occur shortly after the CMB window. Extensions involving reheating through heavy right-handed neutrinos generally require large Yukawa couplings, which induce sizable loop corrections that spoil inflationary dynamics. We show that this tension can be resolved in the presence of supersymmetry and derive constraints on the SUSY breaking scale that allow the mechanism to remain viable within plateau models of inflation. Treating the reheat temperature as a free parameter further enlarges the viable parameter space.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how early QCD confinement induced by inflaton-gluon coupling during inflation affects axion mass, suppresses isocurvature fluctuations, and enables dark matter production, embedding the mechanism in $\alpha$-attractor inflation models and resolving reheating-induced tensions with supersymmetry.
AI.motivation: To explore the impact of early QCD confinement during inflation on axion physics, dark matter production, and inflationary observables, addressing challenges related to isocurvature perturbations and inflationary dynamics.
AI.method: Model early QCD confinement via direct coupling between inflaton and gluons, embed mechanism in $\alpha$-attractor inflation model, analyze parameter space and reheating scenarios, and incorporate supersymmetry to resolve tensions.
AI.result: Demonstrated that early QCD confinement can suppress axion isocurvature perturbations and enable dark matter production post-CMB epoch; QCD corrections shift scalar spectral index; reheating via neutrinos introduces loop corrections remedied by supersymmetry, with constraints on SUSY breaking scale identified.
AI.conclusion: Early QCD confinement during inflation provides a viable mechanism to address axion dark matter abundance and inflation observables within $\alpha$-attractor models, especially when supersymmetry and flexible reheating schemes are included to maintain inflationary consistency.

title: A high-energy neutrino flare associated with nearby bright interacting supernova SN 2021foa
summary: While core-collapse supernovae have been widely discussed as potential neutrino sources, definitive observational evidence has remained elusive. In this work, we report evidence of high-energy neutrino emission in the direction of supernova SN 2021foa, which is one of the closest and brightest interacting supernovae observed to date. Using the second data release of muon track data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, we conducted a time-dependent analysis and identified a neutrino clustering that temporally coincides with the optical peak of SN 2021foa, occurring approximately 16 to 22 days after the discovery date, with a maximum test statistic of $\sim 28.2$. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that the probability of observing such a neutrino excess by chance is $\sim6.7 \times 10^{-5}$, corresponding to a significance of $\sim4.0\,σ$. The spatial and temporal correlation strongly suggests that the neutrinos originate from the supernova. SN 2021foa is a unique "flip-flop" supernova; its spectra repeatedly transitioned between hydrogen-rich (Type IIn) and helium-rich (Type Ibn) phases within 50 days post-peak, reflecting a violent and complex mass-loss history of its progenitor. The inferred neutrino energy exceeds the optical radiative energy and ejecta kinetic energy of the supernova by orders of magnitude, suggesting that the neutrino emission is likely powered by a delayed central engine driving a jet that is choked within the dense circumstellar medium.

AI.tldr: This study reports significant neutrino clustering coincident with supernova SN 2021foa's optical peak, providing strong evidence of supernova-origin high-energy neutrinos likely powered by a central engine jet choked in dense circumstellar material.
AI.motivation: Core-collapse supernovae are theorized as neutrino sources, but no definitive observational evidence has been found.
AI.method: A time-dependent analysis of muon track data from IceCube's second data release was performed, focusing on neutrino clustering in spatial and temporal coincidence with the optical peak of SN 2021foa.
AI.result: A neutrino clustering was identified around the optical peak of SN 2021foa with a test statistic of ~28.2 and significance of ~4.0σ, suggesting the neutrinos originated from the supernova.
AI.conclusion: The observed high-energy neutrino emission correlated spatially and temporally with SN 2021foa provides strong evidence of supernova-origin neutrinos, likely driven by a delayed central engine producing a choked jet in a dense circumstellar medium.

title: What it takes to solve the Hubble tension through Modifications of Cosmological Recombination II: in light of ACT DR6 and DESI DR2
summary: We construct data-driven solutions to the Hubble tension, in light of recent data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT DR6) and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR2). We search for the minimal modification to the recombination history through a time-varying electron mass $m_e(z)$ that increases the best-fit $H_0$ inferred from CMB data toward the SH0ES value, without worsening the fit to the data. Using Planck and ACT data including lensing, we find a perturbative modification to $m_e(z)$ that fully resolves the Hubble tension, with the solution sharing the same qualitative oscillatory structure as in previous work using Planck data alone, demonstrating its robustness to the inclusion of more precise and independent CMB data. As a byproduct, the solution also eases the $S_8$ tension. Once DESI DR2 BAO data are added, however, perturbative modifications to $m_e(z)$ cannot fully resolve the Hubble tension. This reflects the same fundamental limitation: raising $H_0$ by modifying recombination generically lowers $Ω_m$, being inconsistent with late-time cosmological observations.

AI.tldr: Modifying the electron mass during recombination can reconcile CMB and local H_0 measurements using Planck and ACT data, but when adding DESI BAO data, this approach cannot fully resolve the Hubble tension due to inconsistencies with late-time cosmology.
AI.motivation: To address the Hubble tension, the discrepancy between the H_0 value inferred from Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data and local measurements, by modifying the recombination history in a minimal, data-driven way.
AI.method: Introducing a time-varying electron mass m_e(z) that perturbs the recombination history, and fitting this modification against recent CMB datasets (Planck, ACT DR6 with lensing) and BAO data from DESI DR2 to evaluate its effect on the inferred H_0 and S_8 parameters.
AI.result: A perturbative modification to m_e(z) can fully resolve the Hubble tension when using Planck and ACT data, also easing the S_8 tension. However, including DESI DR2 BAO data reveals that such modifications cannot fully resolve the H_0 discrepancy due to conflicts with late-time cosmological parameters, particularly Ω_m.
AI.conclusion: Data-driven, perturbative changes to the electron mass during recombination offer a robust solution to the Hubble tension with high-precision CMB data alone, but are fundamentally limited in resolving the tension when late-time cosmological observations are considered, highlighting a trade-off between raising H_0 and maintaining consistency with other cosmological measurements.

title: Analytic insight into the physics of SASI II. Spiral instability of the prograde mode in a rotating stellar core
summary: During the core-collapse of a rotating massive star, the standing accretion shock instability (SASI) favours the development of non-axisymmetric motions which can imprint specific frequency signatures on the neutrino and gravitational wave signals.This study establishes analytical approximations for the eigenfrequencies of the dominant SASI modes. It also explains the physical mechanism responsible for the further destabilization of prograde SASI modes by differential rotation. A perturbative analysis is used to calculate the eigenfrequencies of a stalled accretion shock in spherical geometry, taking into account the rotation of the collapsing stellar core. The formulation of the perturbative equations as a self-forced oscillator is extended to include differential rotation and interpret the results physically. The oscillation frequency of the dominant mode weakly depends on the detailed formulation of neutrino emission if the shock radius exceeds ~1.5 times the radius r_nabla of maximum deceleration. Analytical expressions are obtained for the one and two-armed spiral modes with a 10% accuracy in this regime. The effect of differential rotation is explained by the role of phase mixing between the advective forcing and the acoustic structure. The radial wavelength of vorticity perturbations associated with the prograde mode is increased by differential rotation, leading to a better phase match with the large radial scale of the acoustic structure. Even when rotation is too modest to involve a corotation radius, its adverse effect on phase mixing can be significant at small radius due to the steep inward increase of the rotation frequency ~1/r^2 in the region of stationary accretion. In the regime of stronger rotation involving a corotation radius, the stationary phase approximation sheds light on the dominant advective-acoustic coupling, located between the corotation zone and the shock.

AI.tldr: This study analytically characterizes the dominant SASI mode frequencies during rotating massive star core collapse, showing how differential rotation enhances prograde mode destabilization through improved phase matching and advective-acoustic coupling, providing frequency predictions relevant for neutrino and gravitational wave signals.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical mechanisms and frequency signatures of the standing accretion shock instability (SASI) during core-collapse of rotating massive stars, particularly how differential rotation affects SASI mode destabilization.
AI.method: Performed a perturbative analysis of eigenfrequencies of stalled accretion shocks in spherical geometry including rotation of the stellar core; extended the perturbative equations as a self-forced oscillator to include differential rotation for physical interpretation.
AI.result: Derived analytical approximations for the eigenfrequencies of dominant SASI modes (one and two-armed spiral modes) with ~10% accuracy for shock radii above ~1.5 times r_nabla; explained how differential rotation increases the radial wavelength of vorticity perturbations, improving phase matching with acoustic structures, enhancing destabilization of prograde SASI modes; identified the role of advective-acoustic coupling in both modest and strong rotation regimes, including effects of corotation radius.
AI.conclusion: The presence and strength of differential rotation significantly influence SASI mode frequencies and stability by modifying phase mixing and advective-acoustic coupling, which can imprint distinct frequency signatures on neutrino and gravitational wave signals during core-collapse of rotating massive stars.
